name: TRAINING_EDITION_1.0_RC1.5
scope: Scoring-rule update: TV rules are now real game rules for the Show profile. Correct answers are clamped to 200–300; wrong answers lose 50–200 based on the leaderboard before the round; first 3 omissions remain free, later omissions inherit the same rank-based wrong penalty.
features: Shared readability engine classifies question load as normal, dense or very dense using question length, total answer text, longest answer and presence of an image
Old single-answer 72-character cutoff removed; dense layout is based on the whole text load
Dense questions keep larger question/answer text and recover space first by shrinking image column, gaps and mascot area
Very-dense questions hide the mascot, reduce side chrome and shrink the image column before reducing text
Questions with images no longer reserve the previous 24% width by default; standard image column reduced to 20%, dense to 15.5%, very-dense to 11.5%
Pack Studio uses the same readability model and displays a warning for dense/very-dense questions
Legacy content remains data-only: no pack CSS/JS can override the Training Edition renderer
Show profile correct-answer points are now clamped to 200–300 (300/275/250/... with minimum 200)
Show profile wrong-answer penalty is dynamic: −200 for the leading score group down to −50 for the last score group, linearly distributed across distinct leaderboard positions
When all teams are tied before a round there is no meaningful ranking, so the wrong-answer penalty starts at the minimum −50
Tied teams share the same wrong-answer penalty
The first 3 omissions remain free; later omissions use the same pre-round leaderboard penalty as a wrong answer
HOST and server both compute the penalty from the leaderboard before the round; historical reopen/recompute uses chronological round order
The TV rules screen reads the active scoring profile and matches the Show profile mechanics
knownLimitations: No full backup/restore from file: manual copy of packs/ and data/ remains documented.
Real projector viewing distance and real tablets on school Wi-Fi remain required manual QA.
A fresh browser E2E was not run in this environment; Chromium CLI visual capture did not complete reliably, so no visual browser pass is claimed.
Extremely long content can still be pedagogically unsuitable even though the renderer now protects text readability more aggressively.
simulatePlayers: 2/6/15/30 devices, 5 rounds each, no lost or duplicated responses; dynamic standings penalties verified (2026-10-10)
manualQA: RC1.5: unit/integration suite and real WebSocket simulator passed. The TV rules screen was not visually re-verified on a physical classroom projector in this environment.
